title: Manatee County Referendum: Environmental Lands Bonds and 0.16-Mill Levy
what_it_does: County ballot question (Yes / No). Passes with a simple majority of votes cast on the question.
ballot_summary: Water quality protection, overdevelopment prevention, natural lands preservation and public preserves general obligation bonds referendum. Manatee County asks voters to authorize up to $75 million in general obligation bonds, repaid by an additional property tax of up to 0.16 mill, to acquire, improve and maintain environmentally sensitive lands, protect drinking-water sources, water quality and wildlife habitat, and provide public preserves.
what_yes_means: A YES vote authorizes up to $75 million in bonds and an added 0.16-mill tax (about $47 a year on a home with $300,000 taxable value, per county estimates) for conservation-land purchases, easements and preserves, building on the 2020 program.
what_no_means: A NO vote means no new bonds or added levy; the county's existing 2020 environmental-lands program continues but without the additional funding.
verified_ballot_note: Ballot title and details as reported by the Bradenton Times (https://thebradentontimes.com/stories/commissioners-approve-an-environmental-lands-funding-referendum-for-the-november-ballot,207005) and Tampa Bay Beacons (https://www.tampabaybeacons.com/2026/07/28/land-preservation-referendum-will-be-on-nov-3-ballot-in-manatee/), July 2026; the County Commission voted 6-0 to place it on the ballot.
